summary: Implemented the accepted ADR-023 F6 mechanism (F4 untouched). (1) Added the bounded DiscardReason enum (ConfigurationStale, ItemMissing, Ineligible, ConnectionChanged, IdentityUnavailable) and WorkProcessingResult.Discarded(reason, description): a discard stays a completed, non-retryable outcome but carries the machine-readable classification; Completed/Transient/Terminal carry none, and an undefined classification is rejected. (2) Classified all 12 MetadataReconciliationProcessor discard sites: both configuration-version checks (the initial check and the pre-publication re-check) are ConfigurationStale; both item-absent sites ItemMissing; the eligibility and no-provider sites Ineligible; the connection sites ConnectionChanged; the identity-creation and subject-mismatch sites IdentityUnavailable. (3) The worker now captures the final result, releases the in-flight slot (CompleteProcessing) in its finally, and only then re-enqueues exactly one fresh LibraryWorkItem at the current configuration version when the result is a ConfigurationStale discard and the processed item's carried version differs from the current version; a non-ConfigurationStale discard, a same-version stale classification, a stopped queue, and a full queue re-enqueue nothing, and the enqueue is non-blocking (bounded drop, never blocked). WorkItemKey, single-flight/coalescing, and the event/webhook/per-item/post-save triggers are unchanged. (4) Mechanism confirmation against the shipped code: a same-key enqueue while the key is in flight returns WorkHintEnqueueOutcome.InFlight and is dropped (LibraryWorkQueue.Enqueue); CompleteProcessing releases the slot by decrementing/removing the key from the in-flight map; before this task the worker released the slot only in its finally after ProcessWithRetryAsync returned, so a re-enqueue issued inside the processing path was coalesced away (the ADR implementation fact, and the reason for the release-first ordering); every discard previously returned the free-text WorkProcessingResult.Completed(reason). All assumptions held; no STOP was needed. interpretations.question: Which mapping do the ADR-023 enum values have at the discard sites the ADR does not name individually (the provider-kind site, the two Jellyfin-item-changed sites, and the two identity-creation sites)?
interpretations.chosen: The no-reconciliation-provider site is Ineligible; both identity-creation failures and the subject-mismatch site are IdentityUnavailable; item-absent (initial and pre-publication) is ItemMissing; connection absent/disabled/changed is ConnectionChanged; both configuration-version checks are ConfigurationStale.
interpretations.basis: The enum is fixed at five bounded values and each value has exactly one natural meaning; only ConfigurationStale ever changes worker behavior, so the remaining mapping is diagnostic only.
interpretations.impact: A bounded diagnostic classification on existing discards; no re-enqueue or persisted-state effect. The provider-kind site is unreachable for currently supported identities because Series/Season fail badge-surface eligibility first, so Ineligible is a defensive classification.

interpretations.question: Does 'the pre-publication version re-check' of ADR-023 clause 1 include the artwork-stage configuration check in ArtworkPublishingWorkItemProcessor (the check after metadata publication and before the artwork decision)?
interpretations.chosen: No. The two version checks classified as ConfigurationStale are the two MetadataReconciliationProcessor checks (the initial check and the re-check immediately before publishing metadata state). The artwork-stage check is not a discard: it returns the successful metadata-publication result, so it remains a success and does not re-enqueue, exactly as before this task.
interpretations.basis: ADR-023 context fact 2 describes every discard as currently returning Completed(reason); the artwork-stage check returns the successful publication result, not a discard. The ADR text names one pre-publication re-check, and the metadata re-check is the one documented as 'immediately before publishing' in the architecture and the code. ADR-023's rejected alternative also requires that the classification come from the processor and must not extend re-enqueueing to successful-but-stale work.
interpretations.impact: The F6 limitation scenario (an item pending or in flight when the save activates the new version) is fixed. The narrow race where the configuration advances between the metadata publication and the artwork stage of the same pass is unchanged from before this task: that pass performs no artwork work, and the artwork applies when the item is next processed by any trigger (the post-save hint for it was coalesced in that window). This is existing behavior, not a new policy, and is recorded as a known limitation.

interpretations.question: Should the worker's stale-basis re-enqueue be attempted when processing was cancelled (host shutdown)?
interpretations.chosen: The single code path is attempted unconditionally after the slot release, but on shutdown the queue has already stopped accepting (StopAsync calls StopAccepting before cancelling), so the attempt is a bounded Stopped drop.
interpretations.basis: ADR-023 clause 3 requires a stopped or full queue to drop the re-enqueue rather than block; adding a cancellation special case would duplicate the queue's own stopped-state contract.
interpretations.impact: No work is enqueued during shutdown; no behavioral difference from an explicit cancellation check for the shipped host lifecycle.
